transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot an immigrant to
New York City late Thursday afternoon
while a young boy was in the man's car. Police say the person who was shot is
conscious and was treated at a nearby hospital.
Reporter Stephen Kestenbaum says the shooting sparked protests and calls for
ICE to leave the city.
Police pushed back protesters as they surrounded a law enforcement vehicle
trying to leave upper Manhattan where the shooting took place. Its window had
been shattered. In a written statement Mirza Ram Mamdani called the shooting
an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation and he demanded that the
president end all ICE enforcement actions in New York. Governor Kathy
Hochul said she expressed outrage in a call with President Trump. The
Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that ICE agents were
attempting to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal
conviction and several arrests. They didn't say why he was shot. For NPR News,
I'm Steve Kestenbaum in New York. The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier is
back home. The Lincoln returned to San Diego Bay Thursday after a record
setting uninterrupted time at sea supporting the Iran war. The extended
deployment drew national attention following reports of conditions on board.
Democratic California Congresswoman Sarah Jacobs was in San Diego to meet
the carrier. I embarked on the ship last week and met with sailors and Marines
directly who told me about their own experiences without being able to get
the mental health care they needed, not being able to get as much food as they
needed, not having access to hot water and some days being able to take a
shower. The Navy initially downplayed any problems and President Trump said that
the Lincoln's lengthy deployment was not nearly long enough. The carrier spent 265
days at sea. As Hurricane Iseas turns into Gulf residents in Mexico Beach on
the Florida Panhandle are thinking back to Hurricane Michael, a category five
storm that crushed the community eight years ago this weekend. Randy Buxto with
member station WFSU's World News Service reports on how that's
influence preparations for this storm. As Iseas continues to head towards
landfall, Miles Magalski, Mexico Beach city administrator says community members
are feeling nervous. He says in years past a hurricane may have been excused
for a party but this time because of Hurricane Michael now I've not heard of
one party being scheduled for this particular Friday night. As of now the
storm is rejected to head north making landfall somewhere between Pensacola and
Alabama but many Mexico Beach residents say the path reminds them of what they
saw with Michael. Now they are preparing for the worst, setting up sandbags,
grabbing supplies and moving vehicles to higher ground. For NPR News, I'm Randy
Buxto in Panama City, Florida. And you're listening to NPR News. The Justice
Department has filed a new indictment against Venezuela's former president and
his wife. The couple now face a torture charge in addition to drug trafficking
NPR's Ryan Lucas reports. Nicolas Maduro and his wife Celia Flores Maduro have
been in US custody since they were captured in an American military raid in
January. The Maduro's were charged with narco-terrorism, drug and weapons offenses
for allegedly working with drug cartels to traffic cocaine to the United States.
They have pleaded not guilty. Now they are facing one additional charge of
torture. Prosecutors allege Maduro used violence including torture to maintain
power in Venezuela. The alleged abuse included electric shock, rape, starvation
and threats to kill victims families. Prosecutors say US citizens were among
those subjected to such measures. The couple is scheduled to go on trial in
June. Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington. President Trump's plan memorial arch is
facing a new lawsuit. The Arlington County Board in Virginia filed the suit
Thursday becoming the first government body to take legal action. The lawsuit
cites what it says is a feverish pace toward construction and says it will
harm public safety and likely require changes to nearby flight paths. The
Norwegian Nobel Committee is preparing to award the Nobel Peace Prize. The prize
is to be awarded in a few hours. The committee and also received nominations
for 287 candidates. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has attracted
attention in prediction markets. I'm Jael Snyder. This is NPR News. This message
